message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “Uno.” | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (red, yellow, green, blue) × 25 cards each (1–9, two of each; plus two “Skip,” “Reverse,” “Draw Two” per color). 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four.” | | **Setup** | Shuffle, deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn** | 1. **Draw** – If you can’t play, draw one card. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately. 2. **Play** – Put a card that matches either color, number, or symbol, or a Wild. 3. **Discard** – You may discard multiple cards of the same value (e.g., three 5’s). | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction (two players → Skip).
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and skips a turn.
• **Wild** – Change the current color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – Change color and next player draws four cards (must be used only if you have no playable card; otherwise you can be challenged). | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you’re down to one card, shout “UNO!” before your opponent takes their turn. If you forget and another player calls it, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all cards. Score: sum of the values of cards left in opponents’ hands (number cards = face value, action cards = 20, Wild = 50). | | **Game End** | First to reach the agreed point total wins. | **Optional Variations** * **Stacking** – Allow players to stack Draw Two/Wild Draw Four cards instead of drawing immediately. * **No Challenge** – Disallow challenges to Wild Draw Four. * **Speed Uno** – Play without drawing; discard as many cards as possible each turn. That’s the core of Uno—simple, fast, and a lot of fun!
